chapters.title: Chapter 2: Before You File: Documents and Pre-Checks

lessons.title: The Pre-Filing Checklist: Bank Accounts, Rent Receipts and Investment Proofs

body.text: You attach no proofs to your ITR. That is exactly why you need them. Every figure you type is a claim, and the department can ask you to back it up long after you click Submit.

children.text: The last two lessons set up your PAN, portal account and tax documents. This one builds your filing folder. Work through four groups in order: bank accounts, rent and salary papers, deduction proofs, and investment statements. Some items matter only in the old regime, and this lesson flags which ones.
Group 1: Every Bank Account You Held

markDefs.definition: An account that has not been operated for more than three years. For ITR purposes, such accounts need not be reported.

children.text: Your ITR asks for details of all savings and current accounts you held in India at any time during FY 2025-26, including accounts you closed during the year. The only exception is a

. For each account you give the bank's IFSC, the account number and type, and you pick one pre-validated account for your refund. Every account also means interest income, and savings account interest has to be reported even though banks do not deduct TDS on it.

body.title: Which Account Can Stay Off the Return?
body.question: Imran, a chartered engineer in Hyderabad, held these accounts during FY 2025-26. Which one does he not need to report in his ITR?
options: An Axis Bank current account he closed in January 2026
An ICICI Bank savings account with a balance of only ₹800, which he used for a single UPI payment in the year
A Bank of India account in his hometown with no transactions since 2020
A joint savings account with his wife at Federal Bank
body.explanation: Only the Bank of India account qualifies as dormant, with no operations for more than three years. A closed account still counts if it was held during the year. A tiny balance does not make an account dormant: he made a payment from it during the year, so it is active. Note that interest credited by the bank on its own does not count as you operating the account. A joint account in which he is a holder is also reported.

children.text: In the old regime, savings account interest qualifies for a deduction of up to ₹10,000 under Section 153 of the Income-tax Act, 2025 (Section 80TTA of the Income-tax Act, 1961). Senior citizens get a higher limit of ₹50,000 that covers FD interest too (Section 80TTB of the 1961 Act, also merged into Section 153). In the new regime, neither deduction is available, so every rupee of interest is taxable.

body.title: Add Up the Savings Interest
body.prompt: Priya is in the old regime. Her passbooks show savings interest for FY 2025-26 of ₹6,200 from SBI, ₹3,900 from HDFC Bank and ₹1,400 from Kotak before she closed that account. She is 29. After the savings interest deduction, how much of this interest is taxable?
body.explanation: Total savings interest is ₹6,200 + ₹3,900 + ₹1,400 = ₹11,500. The deduction for savings account interest is capped at ₹10,000 for someone below 60, so ₹1,500 remains taxable. She reports the full ₹11,500 as income from other sources and claims ₹10,000 as a deduction. In the new regime, all ₹11,500 would be taxable.

children.text: Group 2: Rent and HRA Papers (Old Regime Only)

If you live in rented accommodation, receive HRA and are in the old regime, part of your HRA is exempt under Section 10(13A) of the Income-tax Act, 1961. The ITR now asks for the details behind the claim: your place of work, actual HRA received, rent paid and salary. The exempt amount is the lowest of three figures.

body.latex: \text{HRA Exemption} = \min\left(\text{HRA Received},\; \text{Rent Paid} - 10\%\text{ of Salary},\; 50\% \text{ or } 40\% \text{ of Salary}\right)
body.caption: Salary here means basic plus dearness allowance forming part of retirement benefits, plus any turnover-based commission. 50% applies in Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata and Chennai; 40% elsewhere for FY 2025-26.

body.text: Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Pune and Ahmedabad move to the 50% category under the Income-tax Rules, 2026, but only from Tax Year 2026-27. For the FY 2025-26 return you file in 2026, employees in these four cities still use 40%. Many online calculators have already switched, so check which year yours is built for.

body.caption: Rahul's HRA Exemption: Infosys, Bengaluru, FY 2025-26

cells: Exempt HRA: the lowest of the three

body.text: Notice that Rahul's exemption was decided by the rent limb, not the city limb. Even at 50%, his exemption would still be ₹1,80,000. The metro percentage only matters when it is the smallest of the three numbers, which usually happens when rent is high compared with salary.

body.title: Your Turn: HRA in Chennai
body.prompt: Sana works for an MNC bank in Chennai and is in the old regime. For FY 2025-26, her basic salary plus DA is ₹5,00,000, she received HRA of ₹3,00,000, and she paid rent of ₹22,000 a month. What is her exempt HRA?
body.explanation: Rent for the year is ₹22,000 × 12 = ₹2,64,000. The three limbs: actual HRA ₹3,00,000; rent minus 10% of salary is ₹2,64,000 − ₹50,000 = ₹2,14,000; Chennai is a metro, so 50% of salary is ₹2,50,000. The lowest is ₹2,14,000, which is exempt. The remaining ₹86,000 of HRA is taxable.

body.title: The Landlord PAN Rule
body.textWithBlank: To claim HRA, you must provide your landlord's PAN if the rent you pay in a year exceeds ₹___.
body.explanation: The threshold is ₹1 lakh of rent a year, which is about ₹8,333 a month. Above that, keep the landlord's PAN. Under the new Rules from Tax Year 2026-27, you will also need to disclose your relationship with the landlord.

body.text: Paying rent to a parent who owns the house is allowed, provided the arrangement is genuine: pay through the bank, have a rent agreement, and your parent must report the rent in their own ITR. Rent to a spouse is viewed with far more suspicion. Made-up rent receipts are easy to catch, because the landlord's PAN lets the department check whether that rent ever appeared in anyone's return.

children.text: The ITR no longer accepts one lump sum for your deductions. You select each deduction from a dropdown and enter details such as the type of investment, policy numbers and the insurer's name. Gather these before you sit down to file.

body.caption: Deduction Proofs and What the ITR Asks For

cells: EPF in Form 16, PPF passbook, ELSS statement from CAMS or KFintech, LIC premium receipts, school tuition fee receipts, home loan principal certificate
Type of investment, amount, and policy or account number
Health insurance premium receipts, preventive health check-up bills
Insurer name, policy number, and split between self and parents
Lender's provisional or final interest certificate
Donation receipt and Form 10BE from the charity
Donee's name, PAN, address and amount donated

body.text: In the new regime, you can skip this group almost entirely, since HRA, 80C, 80D and home loan interest on a self-occupied house are not allowed. One exception worth knowing: your employer's contribution to your NPS account is still deductible in the new regime, and it will already be reflected in Form 16.

body.title: Deductions Forgotten at Work
body.scenario: Neeraj, 38, works at a consulting firm in Gurugram and is in the old regime, with taxable income comfortably in the 20% slab. His Form 16 shows ₹1,30,000 under 80C (his EPF) and nothing under 80D. He forgot to tell HR that in FY 2025-26 he also invested ₹20,000 in an ELSS fund and paid ₹38,000 by UPI for a health insurance policy covering his parents, aged 67 and 70.
body.prompt: Can Neeraj still claim these in his ITR? What will he need, and roughly how much tax does he save?
body.modelAnswer: Yes. Form 16 only reflects what he declared to HR; the ITR is where deductions are finally claimed. For 80C, his EPF of ₹1,30,000 plus the ₹20,000 ELSS brings him to exactly the ₹1,50,000 limit. For 80D, his parents are senior citizens, so premiums up to ₹50,000 qualify, and his ₹38,000 is fully deductible. He paid by UPI, which matters, because health insurance premiums paid in cash do not qualify. He needs the ELSS account statement from CAMS or KFintech and the premium receipt showing the insurer name and policy number, since the ITR asks for both. Extra deductions total ₹58,000. At the 20% slab plus 4% cess, the saving is ₹58,000 × 20% × 1.04 = ₹12,064. Since his employer's TDS was computed without these deductions, this will come back to him as a refund.

children.text: Group 4: Investment Income and Capital Gains Statements

This group applies to everyone, in either regime. If you sold a share, redeemed a mutual fund, received a dividend or earned rent, it is already in your AIS. Your job is to match it against your own statements and pick the right ITR form. Any capital gain from selling shares or mutual funds usually takes you out of ITR-1, which Chapter 4 covers in detail.

Dividend report and AIS dividend entries

body.label: MF Central: Consolidated Mutual Fund Statements
body.description: A joint platform of CAMS and KFintech where you can download a consolidated capital gains statement covering mutual fund folios serviced by both registrars.

body.title: The Master Pre-Filing Checklist
steps: List every Indian bank account held during FY 2025-26, including closed ones, and mark any dormant accounts
Note savings interest from each passbook or statement
Confirm which pre-validated account you want the refund in
Old regime: gather rent agreement, rent payment proofs and landlord PAN if rent exceeded ₹1 lakh
Old regime: collect 80C, 80CCD(1B) and 80D proofs with policy numbers, PRAN and insurer names
Old regime: get your lender's home loan interest certificate and any Form 10BE for donations
Download your broker's tax P&L and your consolidated mutual fund capital gains statement
Collect FD interest certificates and any Form 16A
Keep Form 16, Form 26AS, AIS and TIS from the previous lesson in the same folder
Save everything as PDFs in one folder named for FY 2025-26, and keep it well after filing

points: Report every Indian savings and current account held during the year, including closed ones, except dormant accounts not operated for more than three years
Savings interest is taxable even without TDS; the old regime allows up to ₹10,000 (₹50,000 for seniors) under Section 153 of the 2025 Act (80TTA and 80TTB of the 1961 Act)
HRA exemption, old regime only, is the lowest of actual HRA, rent minus 10% of salary, and 50% or 40% of salary; for FY 2025-26, only Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata and Chennai get 50%
Keep a rent agreement, payment proofs, and your landlord's PAN once rent exceeds ₹1 lakh a year
The ITR asks for itemised deduction details such as policy numbers and insurer names, so collect proofs for 80C (Section 123), 80CCD(1B) (Section 124) and 80D (Section 126) before filing
Deductions missed in Form 16 can still be claimed in the ITR, and capital gains, dividends and interest must be matched against broker, registrar and bank statements in either regime

body.text: This lesson is for educational purposes only and does not constitute tax advice. Deduction limits, HRA rules, disclosure requirements and section numbers reflect the position for FY 2025-26 at the time of writing and can change through the Finance Act, the Income-tax Rules or updated ITR forms. Verify with the Income Tax Department's portal or a qualified tax professional before filing.
